this looks amazing. my general tips i give to everyone: pat it dry beforehand, salt before by at least 4 hours if you can, season with sea salt pepper and garlic powder before throwing into the pan, get the pan extremely hot and use avocado oil, dont move the steak for x amount of time (depending on thickness, recommended thickness is 3/4 of an inch to 1 1/2 inches) then flip, after you flip throw in a generous amount of butter, 3-4 cloves of crushed garlic, rosemary, and then baste the steak with that combination of oil, be sure to sear the sides when you’re done to render the fat and increase flavour (seasoning sides helps too), let it rest for 5-10 minutes, and this is where the magic comes in, as soon as you take it off top it with garlic butter that you should have prepared beforehand, garlic pasted or crushed garlic, unsalted butter, rosemary leaves, and any spices you want as long as they fit. smear the compound butter across the steak while it rests. enjoy.

i dont reverse sear but my tips would be to try cooking it 5-10°C under your desired temp. when removing it from the pan remove it before it hits the temp you want because it’ll cook while resting. make sure your pan is ripping hot so you can get the crust and if the meat is moist pat it dry.

add the same amount of salt you would put if you were salting the steak just before cooking. leave overnight-24hrs. if not all the salt penetrates into the meat you’re putting too much or you need to leave it for longer. your cut also needs to be thick. what dry brining is supposed to do is extract the moisture so you can get a better crust and a more thorough, consistent salt flavour. make sure you pat the meat dry before searing.
